items.reason: Both describe strategy shutdown closing the factory-owned shared pool, causing subsequent strategies to commit messages that failed to enqueue after rebalance.
Both identify the background thread invoking Arroyo's commit callback outside the consumer thread, risking races in non-thread-safe commit state.
Both claim that requiring every integer offset to exist blocks commits at legitimate Kafka offset gaps, and propose scanning tracked offsets instead.
Both describe unbounded worker queues and missing submission backpressure allowing queued messages to consume memory without limit.
